title: [finding] getMetaDiagnostics `scannedTypes` still overstates the swept set when a type is benignly skipped — no payload field lets a caller detect partial coverage
body:
Restart-when: any PR touches getMetaDiagnostics in packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts

Filed unassigned by the dev seat on #8855 (PR #8923) to record a residue that card deliberately did **not** close, so it is not lost when #8855 closes. Observation-class: no user-visible failure is claimed today.

## What #8923 closed, and what it left

#8855's ruling was "propagate the 503, no surface change", and #8923 implements exactly that: `getMetaDiagnostics`'s per-type `catch` now rethrows the metadata-store 503 unchanged and still skips the type for every other failure. The **outage** case is therefore loud now.

The residue is the **benign** half of that same `catch`. When a type is genuinely not listable in this kernel scope, the sweep skips it and:

- `scannedTypes` is `targetTypes.length`, fixed **before** the loop and never decremented on `continue`, so the response asserts "I scanned N types" having scanned fewer;
- the discrepancy is **not derivable by the caller** — `Object.keys(stats).length` is only a lower bound, because a type that reads fine but holds no items also produces a `stats` entry with `count: 0`. #8923's own pin measures both spellings of that: 26 stat keys for a clean all-empty sweep, 25 when one type is skipped, with `scannedTypes` reporting 26 in both.

So there is still no field in the payload from which a client can compute "some of this is missing".

## Why it was not fixed under #8855

Triage ruled ([`5302846257`](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/8855#issuecomment-5302846257)) that a per-type degradation marker in the payload is a **public-surface addition**, to be escalated rather than added under that card. #8923 did not conclude the marker was needed — the harm #8855 actually named (an unreadable store published as "0 problems") is closed by the 503 propagation without one. This card is the place to decide whether the benign-skip half deserves the same treatment, not a re-litigation of that ruling.

## What a taker should establish first

The honest open question is whether this is worth any surface at all:

1. **Is the benign skip reachable in practice?** #8923's pin constructs it deliberately (a registry whose listing throws for one type). Whether a real kernel scope produces it — and for which types — was **not** measured. If it is unreachable, `scannedTypes` never actually lies and the right answer is a comment, not a field.
2. If it is reachable, the options are roughly: decrement `scannedTypes` on skip (no new field, but silently changes an existing number's meaning); add a `skippedTypes` list (new public surface, needs the escalation the ruling describes); or leave it and document that `scannedTypes` is an intent count.

Startup-focus applies: no consumer is known to read `scannedTypes` for coverage today — the Studio directory page reads `stats` for tile counts. Establish a reader before adding surface.

## Explicitly not this card

The `organizationId` observation on #8855 (the REST handler forwards `type`/`severity`/`packageId` but no `organizationId`) belongs to the #8805 tenant-scoping thread and was left unmeasured by #8923 per the ruling. It is named here only so nobody re-derives it as new.

Backlinks: #8855, #8923.
